scenes.heading: Moving substances across membranes
scenes.sub: Why does limp lettuce go crisp in cold water?
scenes.say: Every cell has to take in oxygen, glucose and water, and get rid of wastes like carbon dioxide. All of it must cross the cell membrane. Let's see how.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A sausage sizzle smell spreads from the barbecue to the car park
scenes.science: Diffusion: particles spread from high to low concentration
scenes.breaks: smell drifts in open air, but in a cell particles must cross a selectively permeable membrane that only lets some through.
scenes.say: Think of a sausage sizzle. The smell starts strong at the barbecue and spreads out until you can smell it in the car park. That's diffusion: the net movement of particles from high to low concentration, down the concentration gradient. It needs no energy, so it's passive.

scenes.heading: Diffusion is faster when...
scenes.say: Diffusion is faster when the concentration gradient is steeper, the temperature is higher, the distance is shorter, and the surface area is larger.

scenes.heading: Osmosis
points: Diffusion of water across a membrane
Hypotonic: water moves in, cell swells
Hypertonic: water moves out, cell shrinks
scenes.say: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane. Water follows the solute: it moves towards the side with more dissolved stuff. In a hypotonic solution water moves in and the cell swells. Isotonic means no net movement. In a hypertonic solution water moves out and the cell shrinks. Plant cells plasmolyse.

scenes.heading: Potato experiment
scenes.question: Potato cylinders start at 2.00 g. After 24 hours: pure water 2.30 g, 0.4 M sugar 2.00 g, 0.8 M sugar 1.70 g.
lines: Inside of potato cells ≈ 0.4 M sugar
scenes.say: In a potato experiment, cylinders start at two grams. In pure water they gain mass, so the water was hypotonic. In zero point eight molar sugar they lose mass: hypertonic. In zero point four molar there's no change. No change in mass means isotonic, so the inside of the potato cells is about the same as zero point four molar sugar.
scenes.caption: In a potato experiment, cylinders start at 2.00 g. In pure water they gain mass, so the water was hypotonic. In 0.8 M sugar they lose mass: hypertonic. In 0.4 M there's no change. No change in mass means isotonic, so the inside of the potato cells is about the same as 0.4 M sugar.

scenes.heading: Diffusion vs active transport
scenes.say: Active transport is like pumping air into a footy that's already firm. Carrier proteins act like pumps, moving particles from low to high concentration, against the gradient. That takes energy from respiration. Root hair cells taking in mineral ions do this, so they have many mitochondria.

scenes.heading: Surface area to volume
scenes.question: Compare the SA:V ratio of a 1 cm cube and a 3 cm cube.
lines: 1 cm cube: SA 6 cm², volume 1 cm³
3 cm cube: SA 54 cm², volume 27 cm³
scenes.say: As a cell grows, its volume rises faster than its surface area. A one centimetre cube has a ratio of six to one. A three centimetre cube has only two to one. Smaller is better for exchange, which is why organisms are built from many small cells.
scenes.caption: As a cell grows, its volume rises faster than its surface area. A 1 cm cube has an SA:V of 6 : 1. A 3 cm cube has only 2 : 1. Smaller is better for exchange, which is why organisms are built from many small cells.

points: Small cells have a large SA:V ratio
scenes.say: Quick recap. Diffusion and osmosis are passive. In osmosis, water follows the solute. Active transport uses energy to move particles against the gradient. And small cells have a large surface area to volume ratio. Now try the practice questions!
